title: Festive Fare: Gingerbread Stars.
subtitle: Make-at-home treats to gift or enjoy!
description: Our seasonal collection of giftable treats is so delicious, you'll want to keep them all for yourself. Take our gingerbread stars: laced with ginger and mixed spice, and glimmering with white icing, they're sure to light up your festive season!

steps.text: Combine dry ingredients: Line 2 large oven trays with baking paper. Sift 300g (2 cups) plain flour, 1 tbs ground ginger, 2 tsp mixed spice and ½ tsp baking powder into a large bowl. Stir in 220g (1 cup) brown sugar.

Rub in butter: Cut half the butter into cubes. Add to the flour mixture and rub with your fingertips until it resembles fine breadcrumbs. Add the maple syrup and 1 egg and stir with a flat-bladed knife in a cutting action until the mixture just starts to come together. Using clean hands, bring the dough together.
Chill dough: Turn the dough onto a clean surface and gently knead until smooth. Wrap in plastic wrap and freeze for 20 mins or until firm.

Bake gingerbread: Preheat the oven to 180C. Roll out the dough between 2 sheets of baking paper until 5mm thick. Using the cookie cutter, cut out star shapes from the dough, re-rolling the dough as necessary. Put on the lined trays, leaving a 3cm gap between them. Bake, in two batches, for 12-14 mins until just firm to touch. Cool on the trays for 5 mins, then transfer to a wire rack.

Decorate with icing: Meanwhile, put 150g (1 cup) icing sugar and 1 tbs boiling water in a bowl and stir until smooth. Spoon the icing into a medium snap-lock bag and snip off a small corner, then pipe over the cooled gingerbread. Or, simply drizzle over with a teaspoon. Set aside until set. Enjoy! Store in an airtight container for up to 3 days if iced or up to 2 weeks if un-iced. Serves 4.
Make it yours: Get creative with your icing! Squiggle, dot or outline the stars. Or, if you have any edible sprinkles or glitter on hand, scatter over the icing before it sets to add some sparkle.
